newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND NAME HOLLIOAKE BROTHERS AGAINST AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND NAME HOLLIOAKE BROTHERS AGAINST AUSTRALIA.

text.p: England have named brothers Adam and Ben Hollioake in their 15-man squad to play Australia in the three-match one-day series starting at Headingley, Leeds, on Thursday.
Both Adam, 25, and Ben, 19, play for Surrey but, ironically, were born in Australia.
Nasser Hussain, England's vice-captain during the winter tour to Zimbabwe and New Zealand, was omitted from the squad named on Sunday.

Selectors' chairman David Graveney said: "He was considered but we thought that John Crawley, as a good player of leg spin, and Graham Lloyd, who has been in terrific form, were better options although I realise that many people will be surprised by Hussain's omission.'
Adam Hollioake, the new Surrey skipper, was captain of the England A team in Australia this winter but this is the first big chance for Ben. Both are all rounders.

Graveney said: "I have to emphasise that Ben is not along for the ride. We want to send a message that younger players are in contention. He will play a full part in the training on Tuesday and Wednesday and he will be considered along with every other member of the party."

Graveney added: "Adam did well in the series against Pakistan last year and he was an outstanding captain in Australia where Mike Gatting, the coach and now a selector, and I, as tour manager, got to know him well. We look on him as part of the established team."
Ashley Giles, who bowls leg-spinners for Warwickshire, receives his first international call-up while Phil de Freitas, who has not played for England since the World Cup, is also named.

Mike Atherton (captain, Lancashire), John Crawley (Lancashire), Phil DeFreitas (Derbyshire), Robert Croft (Glamorgan), Mark Ealham (Kent), Ashley Giles (Warwickshire), Darren Gough (Yorkshire), Dean Headley (Kent), Adam Hollioake, Ben Hollioake (both Surrey), Nick Knight (Warwickshire), Graham Lloyd (Lancashire), Chris Silverwood (Yorkshire), Alec Stewart and Graham Thorpe (both Surrey).
